chunks: The takbirat al-iftitah is once, and seven times is best.

It is obligatory to recite Bismillahi r-Rahmani r-Rahim aloud in the prayer at the opening of al-Fatiha and at the opening of the surah after it. It is a verse from the Quran, and it is closer to the Greatest Name of God than the black of the eye is to its white.
It is recommended to raise the two hands in every takbira in the prayer, and that is an adornment of the prayer.

key_terms.اسم الله الأعظم: Ism Allah al-A'zam: the Greatest Name of God, believed to hold special spiritual power and whose identity is a matter of scholarly discussion
key_terms.الجهر: Jahr: reciting aloud, as opposed to silent recitation (ikhfat), required in certain prayers according to Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم: Bismillahi r-Rahmani r-Rahim: 'In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' — considered a verse of the Quran and part of every surah except Surat al-Tawba
key_terms.تكبيرة الافتتاح: Takbirat al-iftitah: the opening takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') at the beginning of prayer, also called takbirat al-ihram

ai.seo_question: Is Bismillah a verse of the Quran and should it be recited aloud in prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq contains jurisprudential rulings on prayer practices delivered during the ninety-third assembly in Sha'ban 368 AH. It establishes that the opening takbir (takbirat al-iftitah) is performed once, though seven is preferred, and that Bismillah must be recited aloud before al-Fatiha and the subsequent surah. The text also affirms the theological significance of Bismillah as a Quranic verse closely linked to the Greatest Name of God, using the vivid metaphor of the iris to the white of the eye.

en.bilal-muhammad: The takbirat al-iftitah (i.e. takbirat al-ihram) is once, and seven (times) is best.

Jahr (recitation aloud) with bismillaahi ‘r-rahmani ‘r-rahim is obligatory in the salat at the opening of al-Fatiha and at the opening of the sura after it. It is a verse from the Quran. It is closer to the greatest name of Allah than the black of the eye is to its white.
It is recommended to raise the hands in every takbira in the prayer, and it is the adornment of the prayer.
